properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25, immediately after deciding the adopt nesting step: *"as we defer the functional allocation step in genesis skill (not done at genesis phase), do we need some /system-depth or /functional-allocation skill that the user can use?"*

═══ THE GAP IS REAL AND IT IS PRECISELY LOCATED ═══

**Genesis is RIGHT to defer.** Its line 44 reads: *"Do NOT create Components (P2) yet. Leaving structure unspecified is deliberate: the first DETECT round will surface `concept_without_design`, which is the right next question ('how should this be structured?'). Answer it WITH THE USER, not by guessing."* That is doctrine's function-before-form, correctly sequenced, and it is more disciplined than adopt was until today.

🛑 **AND THEN NOTHING PICKS THE QUESTION UP.** The gap fires, the user is asked "how should this be structured?", and reflow2 offers no method to answer it with. Measured: no served skill mentions functional decomposition, allocation, or `propose_allocation`. So the one step doctrine says produces the architecture is the one step with no guidance attached.

⭐⭐ THE MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS AND NOTHING POINTS AT IT. `propose_allocation` clusters capabilities by weighted coupling into groups — that IS doctrinal step 5, mechanised — and `evaluate_allocation` scores the result for modularity, god components and misplaced capabilities. Both are served tools. Neither appears in any skill. **This is the three-legs failure again** (`fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`): a typed tool with no instruction and no detector-that-notices-absence reaches no user's design, however good it is.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**A. A NEW SKILL — `/allocate` or `/functional-allocation`.** Triggered by `concept_without_design`, or by the user asking "how should this be structured?". It would: decompose capabilities into finer functions where they are compound; run `propose_allocation`; put the proposed grouping to the user rather than applying it; create Components from what they accept; nest them and set `level`; then `evaluate_allocation` and span-of-control as the sanity check.
 ⚠️ Cost: reflow2 has 23 skills and `fact:nine-of-twenty-skills-are-edited-without-a-drift-signal` already measures that the set is hard to keep coherent. A 24th needs to earn its place.

**B. EXTEND GENESIS.** Genesis already owns the deferral, so it could own the return. Cheapest, and it keeps one skill per phase.
 ⚠️ Cost: genesis is the FIRST skill anyone runs and its whole discipline is *stop before structure*. Folding the structuring step back in risks the very thing the deferral protects — a user doing it in one breath, guessing at boxes while the capabilities are still wet.

**C. EXTEND `detect-and-ask`.** The gap already routes there. It is where `concept_without_design` is phrased and put to the user, so the method could live beside the question.
 ⚠️ Cost: that skill is deliberately generic over ALL gaps; giving one gap a bespoke multi-step procedure makes it two skills wearing one name.

**D. NO SKILL — put it in the TOOL DESCRIPTION.** `propose_allocation`'s served description could carry the method, since an agent reading the tool list would meet it at the moment of use.
 ⚠️ Cost: it is only met by an agent that already thought to look for an allocation tool, which is exactly the agent that did not need telling.

**E. A DETECTOR FIRST, SKILL LATER.** Nothing currently notices that a design has capabilities and no components, or components with no allocation. Make the ABSENCE visible, then decide whether the answer needs a skill or a paragraph.
 ⭐ This is the cheapest thing that could not be wrong, and it matches the project's own posture: the loop should ASK rather than wait to be told.

═══ WHAT THE NAME SHOULD NOT BE ═══

Anthony offered `/system-depth` and `/functional-allocation`. **DEPTH IS THE WRONG NAME** and today's work is why: depth is a CONSEQUENCE of allocation, not a thing to go and get. A skill called `/system-depth` would invite the error this session made four times — treating the number of layers as a target rather than as an output that span of control checks afterwards. If it exists, it is about ALLOCATION, and the depth falls out.

📌 AND IT WOULD CLOSE THE SYMMETRY. As of today adopt recovers the structure an artifact HAS (the nesting step, added 2026-08-25). Genesis defers the structure a design NEEDS and nothing derives it. One direction is now instructed and the other is not.
properties.name: SETTLED — option E: make the missing allocation VISIBLE first (`unallocated_component`), and decide about a skill later
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled.

Kept separate from `dec:idea-what-does-se-doctrine-actually-prescribe-upfront-and-what-of-it-does-reflow2-have` (which establishes WHAT doctrine prescribes and which pieces reflow2 owns) and from `dec:idea-does-reflow2-enforce-an-se-process-or-only-supply-the-vocabulary` (which asks whether a design can SHOW it followed a process). This asks a narrower, buildable thing: the one deferred step has no home, and the question is which of five places it should live in — a decision that can be taken without settling either of those.

═══ RESOLVED 2026-08-25 — ANTHONY CHOSE E ═══

Option E over A (a new `/allocate` skill), B (extend genesis) and C (extend detect-and-ask). Built the same day as `cap:unallocated-component-detector` / `req:structure-with-no-function-is-asked-about` (`ce:unallocated-component-detector-2026-08-25`). **The skill question is deferred, not answered** — E's whole point is that the absence is now measurable, so whether a skill is needed can be decided from evidence rather than from taste.

⚠️ **E'S OWN PREMISE WAS HALF WRONG, AND CHECKING IT IS WHAT MADE THE FINDING.** E read *"nothing currently notices that a design has capabilities and no components, or components with no allocation."* The FIRST half was already covered — that is `concept_without_design`, firing at zero components. Only the SECOND half was uncovered, and it was bigger than the option implied: **33 of reflow2's own 95 components** are leaf boxes owning no capability at all, with every detector reporting clean. A recorded option is a hypothesis, not a specification; this one was written by a session that had not measured, and building it as stated would have shipped a redundant check beside a real one.

📌 **THE SYMMETRY #335 OPENED IS NOW CLOSED AT BOTH ENDS.** adopt recovers the structure an artifact HAS. Genesis still — correctly — defers the structure a design NEEDS, and the deferral now has a detector that brings the question back instead of leaving it to whoever remembers. The two interact honestly: recovering a hierarchy MOVES components off the unallocated list by giving them children, because a box that groups other boxes has a job.

⭐ **THE THREE LEGS WERE ALL FITTED, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS DID NOT BECOME ANOTHER `propose_allocation`.** That tool was served, correct, and named in no skill — a typed tool with no instruction and no detector-that-notices-absence reaches no user's design (`fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`). So the detector shipped WITH its row in the detect-and-ask repair table, naming `propose_allocation` and `evaluate_allocation` as the method. Shipping the detector alone would have reproduced the exact failure it was built to fix.

🛑 **WHAT IS STILL NOT ANSWERED.** Whether the allocation step needs a skill of its own. The detector makes the absence countable across real designs; that evidence is what should settle A-vs-B-vs-C, and it does not exist yet.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🔻 LATER THE SAME DAY — TWO THINGS THIS TEXT NOW GETS WRONG, AND A ROAD NOT TAKEN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

❌ **THE "NAMED IN NO SKILL" MEASUREMENT ABOVE IS NOW FALSE, by this PR's own doing.** `propose_allocation` and `evaluate_allocation` are named in the `detect-and-ask` repair row (all three mirrors) as of PR #336, and genesis asks the ility question as of #337. The paragraph is kept because it is WHY the row was added; re-grepping today would contradict it.

❌ **AND THE REPAIR ROW AS FIRST WRITTEN WAS WRONG IN A SPECIFIC WAY.** It named `propose_allocation` as *the* method, which silently hands every user the PERFORMANCE graph — the trap `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph` had predicted seventeen days earlier and which nothing linked to this node until the user remembered it. Corrected in #336's second commit: the row now asks the ility first.

🛑 **THE ROAD NOT TAKEN, recorded with its grounds so it is not proposed again.** After measuring that `propose_allocation` returns 209 clusters for 210 capabilities — because it clusters capability-to-capability `DEPENDS_ON` and the design holds exactly ONE such edge — the agent recommended **building the missing capability-coupling model (the N²/DSM) as the next step**, on the reasoning that the tool cannot work without its input.

**That recommendation was WRONG and was withdrawn the same session.** The N² *is* the performance graph. Building it first would have silently committed reflow2 to performance-driven allocation — the exact failure the four-graphs argument names — while reliability, maintainability and security got no substrate at all. The correct next step was the one the user's own older idea already implied: **ask what the system is FOR before building any allocation machinery**, which is what #337 did.

📊 **THE STATE OF THE FOUR BRANCHES, measured 2026-08-25 and unchanged since 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-21:** maintainability is runnable TODAY (co-change, from ChangeEvents, no instrumentation); performance needs coupling data almost no design declares (1 edge / 210 capabilities on the most heavily modelled design in existence); reliability and security have NO substrate. **A skill that can execute one of its four branches is not a skill yet** — which is the sharpest argument available against option A, and it is an argument from measurement rather than from taste.
